title: The power that divides thought into letters: why speech, the higher, comes last
overview:
Chapter 41 described the levels of thought; chapter 42 asks where the power comes from that divides an idea into combinations of letters. In *bina* an idea is one thing, even in its depth: a car designer thinks "a car". To improve it he must cut it into seats, wheels and screws, and then write it down. That cutting is the five *gevuros* *MNTzPCh* of *Ima*, carved like letters out of a rubber stamp. It looks like a descent, but its root is above the grasp: a baby knows which dish he likes as well as the chef, and cannot say why until he can talk. So "a *katan* has no thought" means no letters of thought.

The combining of the pieces comes from *chachma*, by itself, as long as the speaker keeps the thread of the whole. And speech, rooted in *chachma*, is higher than thought and therefore comes last; that is why teaching and saying the words wake up the thought, and why the symbol comes before the thing: the *Aibershter* wanted *matza*, so He made *Pesach*.

combinations of letters: the idea turned into words, the symbols of thought
division: of an idea into particulars, of thought and of speech into letters
discernment: telling one thing from another, which a baby has before he has words
the power that combines; from chachma, it puts the pieces together automatically
the father founded the daughter: speech, in its root, is from chachma
a minor, said to have no thought: no letters of thought, though he thinks
the intellectual soul, called davka the speaking soul
heretics; here those who say a ritual is just a symbol
the speaking spirit; the soul once it has the letters of speech

sections.title: Where the power to divide thought into letters comes from: the five gevuros of Ima
sections.summary: The chapter asks where the power comes from that divides an idea into combinations of letters in thought. The answer is the five *gevuros* *MNTzPCh* of *Ima*: the *tzimtzum* in *bina* that cuts the one idea into pieces, as letters are carved out of a rubber stamp.

phrases.he: (מב) ומעתה יובן בענין שרש כח המחלק לצירופי אותיות דמחשבה במדריגה הג', כשחושב ענין דבר מה בצירופים שונים, מאין הוא בא כח ההתחלקות זאת
אך הנה ידוע דבחינת ה׳ גבורות מנצפ"ך דאימא הוא שרש כח ההתחלקות הזאת כו'.
וביאור הדברים ידוע, דבחינת אימא הוא בחינת בינה והשגה לאורך ורוחב בהסבר דבר המושכל
וכאשר הוא מעיין בבחינת העומק של ההשגה, עדיין הוא רק בעומק מחשבה עיונית הנזכר לעיל, שלמעלה מהיות בחינת התחלקות צירופי אותיות ממש במחשבה להשכלת הענין,
רק בחינת מחשבה שכל בלבד כנראה בחוש
phrases.en: It's actually the inner *machshava* of the mind; it's not yet actually an external *machshava* of separate letters.

blocks.text: What power divides the letters of thought into combinations? The five *gevuros* (powers of restraint) of *Ima* (the mother), which is *bina* (understanding), grasp in length and breadth. Even its depth is only *machshava iyunis* (analytical thought), the mind's inner thought, **not yet actually an external *machshava* of separate letters**.

phrases.he: אך על ידי בחינת ה׳ גבורות, שהוא בחינת הצמצום והסתלקות שבכח ההשגה עצמה, להיות יורד אור השכלת הענין שבמחשבה עיונית הנזכר לעיל לבחינת התחלקות צירופים שונים בפרטי פרטיות כו'
phrases.en: This brings out, through the power of *tzimtzum* of *bina*, the ability to cut it up into particular *inyanim* that can be analyzed.

phrases.he: והוא הנקרא בחינת ה׳ גבורות מנצפ"ך דאימא, שנקרא פתוחי חותם כו'
phrases.en: This is what's called the five *gevuros* of *Ima*, *pituchei chosam*: the *pituchim* of the seal, carve out the seal.

blocks.text: The five *gevuros* are the *tzimtzum* (contraction) within the power of grasp. The inner thought is about the idea as a whole; the *tzimtzum* of *bina* brings out **the ability to cut it up into particular *inyanim* that can be analyzed**.

blocks.title: The rubber stamp
blocks.text: This is *pituchei chosam*, the carvings of a seal, like the bank's rubber stamp for the back of a check: a plain piece of rubber with the letters carved out of it.

The idea is one main thing in the mind, even in the *omek hamusag* (depth of the concept) not yet cut up. Not as in *chachma* (wisdom), an *ayin* (nothing), but as a *yesh* (something), an actual understanding.

blocks.title: Addition
blocks.text: You think of addition as one thing. Only to explain it to somebody, or to yourself when you think up new ways or deeper matters in it, must you be *metzamtzem* (contract): keep some parts and cut others away. That is how a stamp's letters are made.
So a *machshava iyunis* has to dress itself in the external thought of letters; the real *machshevas sechel* (thought of the intellect), before that, is one singular thing.

blocks.title: The car designer
blocks.text: A car designer thinks of a car as a car, just as someone who knows nothing about cars does, though he knows far more. It is one holistic idea, not analyzed yet, as a listener put it: the *tamtzis* (essence), the *omek hamusag*. When he sits down to next year's model, improvements to make a few million dollars on, the whole car is first in his mind as a *tamtzis*.

blocks.title: The car designer
blocks.text: A *tamtzis*, not a *kitzur*: the *kitzur* (shortening) is the short idea before the *iyun* (analysis), the *tamtzis* the idea after it. Still, to design a better car he must cut it into teeny pieces. He cannot think real hard, meditate, do his breathing exercises, and poof, here is the 2005 model. He takes it into components: the seats, the wheels, their screws and material, the grooves; maybe we should change the grooves.
That is the *MNTzPCh* of *bina*: the *gevuros* make *tzimtzumim*. To think about the seat he cuts away the car, as a seal's letter is left by cutting around it.

sections.title: Cutting the idea into letters looks like a descent, but its root is above the grasp
sections.summary: Bringing the whole idea down to pieces, and then to letters, looks like a descent, yet the power to do it is rooted higher than the grasp of the idea itself. The proof is a small child, who can tell one thing from another before he has letters in his thought.

phrases.he: ואף על פי שלכאורה בחינת ירידה וצמצום הוא,
phrases.en: At first glance it looks like really a *yerida* and a *tzimtzum*.

phrases.he: אבל שרשו בא מלמעלה מכח ההשגה שבגוף המושכל הזה כו'
phrases.en: The fact that he can do that is higher than even the actual *sechel* of the car itself.

blocks.text: **At first glance it looks like really a *yerida* and a *tzimtzum***: from the *tamtzis* of the whole car down to a seat. But its root is above the grasp of the idea itself.

To improve the car, thinking is not enough: he must bring it down to letters and write a report, notes to himself or to other car geniuses. **The fact that he can do that is higher than even the actual *sechel* of the car itself.**

phrases.he: וראיה לזה ממה שאנו רואים בתינוק קטן שאין בו עדיין צירופי אותיות במחשבתו בדבר פרטי כמו גם דבר מה שנותנין לו,
הגם שמבחין בו
phrases.en: He does have the *havchana*.

phrases.he: ולא יחליפנו בדבר אחר כנזכר לעיל,
phrases.en: He likes *davka* this one.

phrases.he: שזה הוא התחלקות המחשבה,
phrases.en: He does have the *hischalkus hamachshava* of *bina*.

phrases.he: אבל לא בצירופי אותיות כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: But not all the way to bring it out into an external *machshava*.

phrases.he: הנה מכל מקום
phrases.en: Nonetheless,

phrases.he: כאשר יכול לדבר ולבקש בפה לדבר פרטי,
phrases.en: Once he already can talk and ask with his mouth for a particular thing,

phrases.he: הרי אז יש לו בודאי במוח מחשבתו צירופי אותיות פרטיים לאותו דבר פרטי שמבקש בדבור

blocks.title: The toy car
blocks.text: The proof is a small child. Give him a toy car: he likes this one and not that one, so he can tell the difference, but he cannot say why, though there is a reason. Toy designers look for those reasons: know why the boys like this car and the girls that doll, and you can make a lot of money.

So the child has the essential *sechel*, the very thing the toy designers study, though he cannot break it into explanations. He likes this car and not that one: the *havchana* (discernment) of *bina*, as in "Who gave the rooster *bina* to distinguish between day and night."

He has the *havchana*, likes this one *davka* (precisely) and has the division of thought, **but not all the way to bring it out into an external *machshava***. **Once he already can talk and ask with his mouth for a particular thing**, he surely has its letters.

sections.title: The letters are divided in thought before speech, and speech is what divides them
sections.summary: To speak, a child must first have the letters divided in his thought; yet it is speech that brings about the division of thought: the voice of the turtledove is heard in speech, and the mother lends her clothing to her daughter. The class opens on direct and symbolic thought.

phrases.he: כי צירופי אותיות מתחלקות במחשבה תחלה טרם בואם לדבור
phrases.en: The *tzirufei osios* has to be separated out in the mind first before you can talk.

phrases.he: (כמו שיתבאר דעקבי לאה נכנסין תוך ראש רחל, דהיינו דבור שבמחשבה הנזכר לעיל שנעשה מחשבה לדבור כו')
וכמו שכתוב במקום אחר בענין מאמר הזהר על פסוק וקול התור נשמע בארצינו,
דוקא בבחינת הדבור
phrases.en: It's heard *davka* in *dibur*: the voice of the inner *machshava* of the thing is heard *davka* in the *dibur*.

phrases.he: אז זמן התחלקות אותיות המחשבה כו'
phrases.en: It's *davka* the *dibur* that brings about the *hischalkus* of the *machshava*.

phrases.he: (והיינו ענין כללות המאמר דאימא אוזיפת דרך שאלה ה׳ גבורות מנצפ"ך לברתא,
phrases.en: This is the general *inyan* of what it says, that the mother loans her clothes in a way of a loan, the five *gevuros*, to her daughter,

phrases.he: שהוא צירופי התחלקות אותיות הדבור כו')
phrases.en: which is the putting together of the separations of the letters of speech.

blocks.title: Just a symbol
blocks.text: What the chapter is about is direct thought against symbolic thought. People say, "Oh, that's just semantics." In matters of *frumkeit*, the Reform and people like that try to reduce these things to a symbol: *Pesach* and the *matzos* are just a symbol, so why make such a big deal of it? Of course, sit down and eat *matza*, and then drink a beer; the main thing is that you did the symbolism. The general idea is that the rituals of religion are just symbols. It is also the universalism of the Greeks, the matter of *Chanuka*: all religions are really the same, except you use these symbols and I use these.
blocks.outOfPlace: Opens class 215, before line 11 is read: it introduces what the chapter is about.

sensitivity.reason: Mocks the Reform view of ritual (eat matza, then drink a beer).

The main thing, they say, is that you did the symbolism. The general idea is that the rituals of religion are just symbols. It is also the universalism of the Greeks, the matter of *Chanuka*: all religions are really the same, except you use these symbols and I use these.

blocks.text: That is the text's subject: letters in a certain order standing for a concept. A child has the concept before he can put it in letters, so the symbolic ability comes from higher than the *etzem* (essence) of thinking.
blocks.outOfPlace: The opening of class 215, just before it reads line 11.

blocks.text: Since he talks, he has *tzirufei osios* (combinations of letters) in mind: **the *tzirufei osios* has to be separated out in the mind first before you can talk**; the heels of Leah enter the head of Rachel. As the *Zohar* says on "the voice of the turtledove is heard in our land," the inner thought **is heard *davka* in the *dibur***: speech brings about the division of thought.
So **the mother loans her clothes in a way of a loan**, the five *gevuros*, **to her daughter**: the letters of speech, combined and divided.

sections.title: The combinations are rooted above the grasp, and Abba puts them together by itself
sections.summary: A baby tastes as well as a chef but cannot say why: dividing an idea into letters is rooted above the grasp of *bina*, in the source of its depth. Putting the pieces together comes from *chachma*, the power that combines automatically, which is why a speaker who loses the whole loses his thread.

phrases.he: ואם כן מזה ראיה שאין הצירופים שרשם בהשגה עצמה
phrases.en: From this, we see that the *tzirufim*, turning the concept into the symbolic words, are not really rooted in the actual understanding itself.

phrases.he: שהרי התינוק מבחין ומשיג בין טוב לרע גם טרם שיכול לדבר,
phrases.en: He already can tell you the difference between things, what he likes and what he doesn't like.

phrases.he: ואף על פי כן אין לו צירופי אותיות במחשבתו עד שיכול לדבר דוקא כנזכר לעיל

blocks.text: So the *tzirufim* **are not really rooted in the actual understanding itself**: before a child can talk, **he already can tell you the difference between things, what he likes and what he doesn't like**.

blocks.title: The baby and the chef
blocks.text: A baby tastes a food and knows at once it is fantastic, and that another he doesn't like. In the *hasaga* (grasp) he knows what the chef knows, every nuance of the taste. He cannot separate it into pieces; the chef can, because he reaches higher than the *hasaga*, down to a recipe: a little cumin, a tiny drop of lemon. The child tastes the cumin and the lemon and likes them; he just doesn't know what they are.

blocks.title: The baby and the chef
blocks.text: Give him the same dish from a chef who did not follow the recipe, and he says, "Eh, that's not so good," as surely as any grown-up. So the division comes from higher: breaking it into pieces, then symbolizing them in written words. The word "cumin" is not the cumin; the cumin itself even the kid can taste.
Still, he has no combinations of letters in his thought until he can speak, *davka*. The class stops over a gap in the printed text before *davka*.

phrases.he: אלא שרשם מלמעלה מן ההשגה דבינה,
phrases.en: The *shoresh* of the actual separation into letters is higher than the actual *hasaga*, the actual understanding of what the concept is all about.

phrases.he: והוא מבחינת כח ומקור של כל עומק ההשגה כו'
phrases.en: It is really from the *koach* and *makor* of that whole depth of the *hasaga*.

phrases.he: (כמו שבאותיות הדבור שרש כח הצירופים מאבא, דהיינו מפנימיות החכמה, שהוא כח המשכיל דחכמה שנקרא קדמות השכל (כמו שכתוב במקום אחר בענין תרין ציפרין כמו שיתבאר בעזרת השם)

blocks.text: The *shoresh* (root) of the division into letters is above the *hasaga* of *bina*: **it is really from the *koach* and *makor* of that whole depth of the *hasaga***. As speech's combinations are rooted in *Abba* (the father), the inside of *chachma*, this lies in the depths of the *koach hamaskil* (the power that brings insight), above *bina*.

phrases.he: ואף על פי שה׳ גבורות מנצפ"ך שבה' מוצאות הוא המחלק ומסדר הצירופים בדבור כפי אופן התחלקות צירופים שבמחשבה, ממש מה׳ גבורות דאימא הנזכר לעיל
מכל מקום אבא יסד
phrases.en: *Davka* the *chachma* is what puts together the speech.

phrases.he: בבחינת כח המצרף, שהוא בלתי כוונה בשכל והשגה איך לצרף, רק ממילא בא,
phrases.en: You don't have to put it together then. It comes together automatically.

phrases.he: וכמו שכתוב מצרף לחכמה וכמו שכתוב במקום אחר וכמו שיתבאר

blocks.text: *Ima*'s *gevuros* order speech's combinations as divided in thought, yet *Abba yasad*: **the *chachma* is what puts together the speech**, as the *koach hamatzref* (the power that combines). Thinking what to say, you only separate, with *bina*. **You don't have to put it together then. It comes together automatically.**

blocks.title: Taking apart a watch
blocks.text: Take apart a watch and you must figure out how to put it back. Even there *chachma* comes from *bina*: take it apart properly, noting how you did it, and you will automatically know how to reassemble it.

A teacher in class thinks how to separate out the matters. You would think he must also think how to put them back into a coherent whole, or end up with little pieces of a car and no car. But he only thinks how to take it apart; it gets put together automatically, the pieces following one another. Not that *chachma* does nothing: its work is automatic.

blocks.title: The thread of thought
blocks.text: As he says later, it is like a necklace, pearls on a string: in English, the thread of thought. A person who loses the thread has lost sight of the whole idea, and it falls apart; he has the next little piece in mind but cannot say it, because he no longer remembers how the whole holds together.

Some places say memory comes from *chachma*; Rabbi Markel does not know just how, or where in the brain. While *bina* cuts the idea up, *chachma* remembers the whole: talking about seats, you remember it is a car.

People go off on a tangent and then ask, "Wait, what were we talking about?" The tangent fit into some whole, but he forgot the whole; and sometimes it goes totally outside the whole, and he literally cannot bring it back.

sections.title: Why a small child is said to have no thought
sections.summary: The combinations come through the *tzimtzum* of analytical thought, but the power that makes them is above that thought. So a child cannot think in words until he can speak, and "a *katan* has no thought" means no letters of thought, not no thinking.

phrases.he: ונמצא שגם שבחינת הצירופים עצמם שבמחשבה על ידי בחינת צמצום דמחשבה עיונית הוא בא, מכל מקום כח ושרש העושה לצירוף והתחלקות זאת,
הרי הוא למעלה מכח ההשגה שבמחשבה עיונית עצמה כו'
phrases.en: It's really higher than the *hisbonenus* itself.

phrases.he: שלזה הטעם אין התינוק יכול לצרף אותיות מחשבתו עד שיוכל לצרף אותיות הדבור,
phrases.en: Until he can talk he can't think in words either.

phrases.he: גם שמשיג ומבחין היטב בגוף הענין דבר מה כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: Even though he understands very well the actual whatever it is.

phrases.he: ואם כן הרי מה שאמרו דקטן אין לו מחשבה,
היינו בבחינת צרופי אותיות המחשבה דוקא,
phrases.en: Meaning that he cannot think in words.

phrases.he: לפי ששרשם בא מכח ומקור של המחשבה דהשגה דבינה כו' ודי למבין

blocks.text: Their power is **really higher than the *hisbonenus* itself**, though they come by the *tzimtzum* of *machshava iyunis*. So **until he can talk he can't think in words either**, though he grasps the thing well. A *katan* (minor) has no thought: not that he can't think, since he knows this from that, but he cannot think in words, whose root is the source of *bina*.

sections.title: Why thought comes before speech: the higher the root, the later it is revealed
sections.summary: Speech is rooted in *chachma* and thought in *bina*, yet thought comes first, in a child and even in the essence of the soul, because what is higher in its root is revealed last. So speaking wakes up the thought, and the symbol comes before the thing.

phrases.he: (וזהו מן הדברים הנפלאים וסתומים,
phrases.en: This is an amazing, wondrous, and hidden thing:

phrases.he: למה המחשבה קדמה לדבור,
phrases.en: Why does thought precede speech?

phrases.he: הרי הדבור שרשו בפנימיות ומקור החכמה והמחשבה שרשה בפנימית ומקור דבינה, והחכמה קדמה לבינה שהחכמה נקרא אין ובינה יש כו'
phrases.en: The speech comes from *chachma* and the *machshava* comes from *bina*.

phrases.he: (וכמו שכתוב במקום אחר בענין דבר ואמרת,
שהדבור גבוה בשרשו מאמירה דמחשבה כו'
phrases.en: The *dibur* first comes before the actual *amira* of *machshava*.

phrases.he: וגם מזה עצמו ראיה ממה שאין המחשבה באה בהתחלקות צרופים כי אם בבוא התחלקות הדבור בתנוק כו׳)
phrases.en: It's *davka* when you learn to talk that's when you learn to think, and not the other way around.

blocks.text: **This is an amazing, wondrous, and hidden thing**: why does thought precede speech? Speech is rooted in *chachma*, called *ayin*, thought in *bina*, called *yesh*, and *chachma* comes first; as on "*Daber v'amarta*" (speak and say), speech is higher in its root than thought. And the child proves that **it's *davka* when you learn to talk that's when you learn to think, and not the other way around**.

phrases.he: ואף על פי כן ה׳ גבורות מנצפ"ך דבינה דוקא שרש לה׳ גבורות התחלקות דדבור, דאימא אוזיפא כו'
phrases.en: Nonetheless, it's *davka* the division in thought that brings about the division in speech.

phrases.he: וכמו שכתוב כאמה בתה כו'
phrases.en: Like mother, like daughter: like the thought that's going to be the speech.

phrases.he: ובשרשם הרי הדבור בחכמה, ולכך אבא דוקא יסד ברתא כו'

blocks.text: Even so, **it's *davka* the division in thought that brings about the division in speech**: like mother, like daughter. Yet speech's root is in *chachma*: *Abba yasad b'rata*, the father founded the daughter.

phrases.he: וגם מצד שרש הראשון דמחשבה דבור ומעשה כמו שהם קבועים בעצם הנפש הנזכר לעיל, (באות ל"ז) שמבואר שם ג' מדריגות הנזכר לעיל במחשבה שבגלוי כו',
הרי גם שם כלול תחלה אותיות המחשבה בעצם הנפש טרם שכלולה מאותיות הדבור שנקרא רוח ממללא כו'
phrases.en: Even in the *etzem* of the soul with the *hiyuli* letters, the letters of *machshava* precede the letters of speech.

phrases.he: דכמו שבנפש שבאה בגוף קדם המחשבה לדבור ב' שנים, כך בנפש הרוחנית לא נקרא רוח ממללא זמן מה כו'
phrases.en: When the soul is forming, it starts off with letters of thought, and the letters of *dibur* come in later, and only then it can be called the full soul.

phrases.he: והמחשבה כבר יש בה כו'
phrases.en: It already has thought.

blocks.text: So too in the essence of the soul (chapter 37): **even in the *etzem* of the soul with the *hiyuli* letters, the letters of *machshava* precede the letters of speech**, though you would expect the opposite there, since speech causes thought, and though the soul is called *ruach memalela* (the speaking spirit).
As thought comes two years before speech in the body, **when the soul is forming, it starts off with letters of thought, and the letters of *dibur* come in later**.

phrases.he: אם לא שכל דבר הגבוה בשרשו בעצמיות יותר הוא בא באחרונה יותר, שלזה נקרא נפש המדברת דוקא נפש המשכלת,
phrases.en: Whatever is higher in its root comes down farther in actuality. That's why the *nefesh hamaskeles*, the thinking person, is called *davka* the talking person.

phrases.he: שזהו בחינת החכמה העצמיות שבה שהוא קודם למחשבה העצמיות שבה כו'
אבל בגלוי בא באחרונה דוקא,
phrases.en: But in revelation, it comes later.

phrases.he: מטעם המבואר במקום אחר באריכות ודי למבין)

blocks.text: Unless **whatever is higher in its root comes down farther in actuality**. So the *nefesh hamaskeles* (the intellectual soul) is called *davka* the speaking soul: its essential *chachma* precedes its thought, **but in revelation, it comes later**. The source of speech is higher than thought.
On this phone call he has to think *davka* because he wants to talk. Had he sat thinking about these very matters before, not trying to say them, it would have woken up no new letters.

So the Rebbe says that teaching somebody else helps you a thousand times more: having to say it and explain it turns your brain on. In *talmud Torah*, say the words, *davka*: you think clearer and hold the train of thought more easily, since speech is connected directly to *chachma*. It is also why learning *b'chavrusa* is better: you talk it over.

blocks.question: Is this also why the *Aibershter* created the world, because it brings it out?
blocks.text: Yes, that is *dibur*: *Ana Emloch* (I shall rule). Speech brings things out, and that is *Malchus* (kingship): bringing it out to somebody else brings out the inner essence.

blocks.title: Matza before the Exodus
blocks.text: This also answers the *minim* (heretics) with their "it's just a symbol," as if the symbol were lower than the thing. It is the opposite. They think *Pesach* happened, so we made up symbols for it; in fact the *Aibershter* (the One Above, G-d) wanted certain symbols and made *Pesach* for them. The proof: they ate *matza* before they left. Leaving too fast for the dough to rise explains why we eat it, not why they ate it there. The *Aibershter* wanted *matza* from the start: the symbol precedes the thing.
That was the point of an earlier question: besides the external name that follows a thing, there is the internal name that makes it.

blocks.title: The carpenter and the table
blocks.text: Those who say otherwise do not do a proper *hisbonenus*. A couch, a chair, a table are things, not symbols? Yes, and each has a name, and the man who made your table had to have "table" in his head first, or he could not have made it. Tell a carpenter to just make something and you'll name it afterwards, and he will ask how he is to know what to make: give him the symbol first.

So the Torah preceded the world, which is made by its words. Likewise *Pesach* was created for the *matza*: one of the 613 commandments, the limbs of the King, *gufa d'malka* (the body of the King), which preceded the story of *Pesach*.

reviewQuestions.question: What are the five *gevuros* *MNTzPCh* of *Ima*, and what does the rubber stamp show about them?
Why does cutting the car into seats and wheels look like a descent, and why is the power to do it higher than the grasp of the car?
What does the baby who knows which chef's dish he likes show about where the combinations of letters come from?
Why does a speaker only have to think how to take an idea apart, and what happens when he loses the thread?
If speech is rooted in *chachma*, why does thought come first, and what does this say about teaching and saying the words aloud?
